problem_title: Lowest Common Ancestor in Binary Tree
input_contract: Input is a family tree with nodes and edges, plus two query nodes p and q. Output the id of the lowest common ancestor node as a string.

variants.name: Post-order DFS with boolean flags
variants.strategy: Recursively explore subtrees, returning whether p or q is present. When both are found in different subtrees or current node is one target and the other found in a subtree, current node is LCA.

pseudocode: Find root and build child map
Post-order DFS: collect found p/q flags from children
If both flags true and LCA not set, mark current node as LCA

variants.name: Path comparison
variants.strategy: Find paths from root to p and q, then compare them to find the last common node.

pseudocode: Find path from root to p via DFS
Find path from root to q via DFS
Compare both paths to find last common node
Find root and build child map
Post-order DFS: collect found p/q flags from children
If both flags true and LCA not set, mark current node as LCA

interaction.prompt: Why does the algorithm backtrack from node 6 when searching for q=1?
options: Node 6 is not the target and has no children

interaction.answer: Node 6 is not the target and has no children
interaction.explanation: Node 6 ≠ target 1 and it is a leaf, so there is no way forward; DFS must backtrack to parent 5.
interaction.wrong_explanation: The issue is not that it was already visited—it was the first visit. The dead end is because it's a leaf not equal to the target.

option_explanations.Node 6 is not the target and has no chil: Correct. A leaf that does not match the target forces backtracking.
option_explanations.Node 6 is the target but already visited: Incorrect. Node 6 is not target 1, and it has not been visited before.

teaching.what: Target not found; node 6 is dead end, backtrack.
teaching.why: Node 6 is not target and has no children, so DFS must pop this node and try other branches.
